newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures rallied to a new contract high on Thursday on the back of a supportive U.S. bond market, hopes for lower interest rates in Europe and relief that no long-dated Bunds will be issued in the fourth quarter.

The December future got its first major boost as Bunds rallied when the Bundesbank said it would not issue 10- or 30-year bonds until the beginning of 1997, forcing the contract through resistance at 124.62/64, traders said.
A surprise 50 basis point cut in the Swiss discount rate helped the contract move up to 124.92 before a positive start to the U.S. session and weak U.S. data sparked a further rally.
The contract stalled however, just below 125.00, and then drifted lower with Bunds on profit taking to settle up 26 centimes at 124.78.
With 175,060 contracts traded, the session was the busiest since September 13.
In the cash market, traders said there was still good buying of long-dated strips by domestic investors, especially around the 15-year area of the curve.
The 10-year spread over Bunds remained steady at three basis points although the two-year spread narrowed five basis points and the 30-year spread narrowed to parity.

The other main event was the return of French welfare debt repayment fund CADES to the franc market. The fund issued 12 billion francs of 6.0 percent 2005 bonds at a spread of seven basis points over OATs.
Members of the syndicate said the sale had gone relatively well given the fact the market had climbed so high today, although the generous pricing had certainly helped.

Some said the consensus among syndicate banks on Wednesday was for a spread of six basis points over OATs, but the bond market rally prompted a reassessment today and the wider spread ensured there was more widespread demand.

There was little reaction to French consumer spending figures released today. Economists said the sharp three percent rise in August was fuelled by car sales, driven by a government incentive, but there were signs of strength in other areas.

Valerie Plagnol, economist at Credit Commercial de France, said although the trend in consumption was upwards, it was a fragile upturn and that the trend in interest rates was still definitely downwards.
She said that with the jobless rate at an all-time high of 12.5 percent, the unemployment figures for August due to be released on Friday would be more important.
PIBOR contracts extended their recent rally, the December contract reached a new contract high at 96.31, outperforming Euromarks slightly.
The franc remained relatively well supported, moving close to 3.3800 per mark late in the session from a low of 3.3847 today and 3.3872 on Friday.
Call money was unchanged at 3-3/8 1/2 percent.
